column1: # NFTBan AI co-author trailer registry (v1.231.0, Lane E)
# DECLARED AUTHORITY for scripts/ci/check-ai-coauthor-trailers.sh. The guard
# reads THIS FILE; it hardcodes no identity of its own. Enforcement and policy
# cannot silently diverge because there is only one place to change.
# POLICY SOURCE — AI_ASSISTED_DEVELOPMENT.md, "Commit metadata policy":
#     Commit metadata MUST NOT credit AI tools as authors. Do not add
#     `Co-Authored-By: Claude`, `Co-Authored-By: ChatGPT`, or any equivalent
#     AI/`OpenAI`/`Anthropic` co-author trailer to commits going forward.
# The four prohibited identities below are the FOUR THE POLICY NAMES IN TEXT:
# Claude, ChatGPT, OpenAI, Anthropic. Nothing else is listed.
# ⛔ DECLARED GAP — NOT SILENTLY WIDENED. The policy's closing clause, "or any
# equivalent AI ... co-author trailer", is an open category, not an enumerable
# list. A guard cannot derive "equivalent AI tool" from the text without
# inventing policy (is `Copilot` an AI tool? `Gemini`? a fine-tuned internal
# model with a product name?). Widening the registry on a CI author's judgement
# would make the machine the policy holder. So: this registry enforces exactly
# what the policy NAMES, and any further identity is added HERE, deliberately,
# by whoever also edits AI_ASSISTED_DEVELOPMENT.md. An unlisted AI identity is
# a POLICY gap, not a detector bug.
# ⛔ SCOPE IS THE CO-AUTHOR TRAILER. `Claude-Session:` and similar provenance
# trailers are NOT co-authorship claims and are NOT prohibited by the policy
# text; they are out of scope here. Prose that merely mentions an AI tool is
# likewise out of scope — the subject of this gate is git trailer syntax.
# ⛔ POPULATION IS THE INCOMING PR RANGE (BASE..HEAD) ONLY. Historical commits
# keep their legacy trailers; the policy says history is NOT rewritten.
# MATCHING
#   - Only lines whose key matches git trailer syntax for the co-author token
#     are considered (case-insensitive, leading whitespace and whitespace before
#     the colon tolerated). Substring matches in ordinary prose are ignored.
#   - `pattern` is a POSIX ERE matched CASE-INSENSITIVELY against the trailer
#     VALUE (everything after the colon).
#   - `class=allowed-automation` is evaluated FIRST and exempts the line. These
#     are real automation identities, not authorship claims by an AI tool.
#   - A human contributor who is genuinely named Claude is not an AI tool: add
#     them as an `allowed-automation`-style exemption row here (class
#     `allowed-human`) rather than weakening a prohibited pattern.
# class<TAB>pattern<TAB>label<TAB>note
allowed-automation
